record.original_question: For an integer d>=3, let D_d(n) be the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set in R^d. Determine the asymptotic order of D_d(n).

artifact.self_contained_problem: For an integer $d \geq 3$, let $D_d(n)$ denote the minimum, over all sets $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of $n$ points, of the number of distinct Euclidean distances $|\{\|p-q\|_2 : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\}|$ determined by $P$. Determine the asymptotic order of $D_d(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. In particular, the standard conjecture asserts that $D_d(n) = \Theta(n^{2/d})$ (with possible polylogarithmic factors); prove or disprove this, and otherwise establish the correct asymptotic growth rate of $D_d(n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct distances problem remains open for every $d \geq 3$. The conjectured bound $\Omega(n^{2/d})$ has not been established. The best known lower bounds are due to Solymosi–Vu (2008), giving roughly $\Omega(n^{2/d - 2/(d(d+2))})$, with $\Omega(n^{3/5})$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$; these still fall short of the conjecture. Recent work (e.g., 2025 arXiv preprints on distinct directions and distances in $\mathbb{R}^d$) confirms the problem is still active and unresolved.
